children: According to CNBC, insurance experts say many U.S. homeowners are underinsured and may not realize it, leaving them exposed to losses from disasters such as wildfires, hurricanes and flooding. Kenneth Klein, a law professor at California Western School of Law, wrote that more than 70% of homeowners in a review of 74,000 California fire-related claims from 2018 to 2023 were underinsured by an average of roughly 20%. He also said about 90% of owner-occupied homes in the U.S. are insured, but many policies exclude or cap coverage for certain disasters, rebuilding costs and specific items.

Experts said flooding is one of the biggest gaps because standard homeowners policies generally do not cover flood damage, which requires separate insurance. The Federal Emergency Management Agency said one inch of water can cause about $25,000 of damage, average flood claim payments were $82,614 between 2020 and 2024, and less than 4% of U.S. households had bought a National Flood Insurance Program policy, according to a 2025 agency blog post. California Insurance Commissioner Ricardo Lara urged consumers to review coverage and consider flood insurance ahead of a likely historic El Niño, noting flood insurance generally takes effect 30 days after purchase.

title: Homeowners Face Widespread Insurance Gaps, Experts Say
